responses.content: {"step": 1, "files": ["report.py", "README.md", "inventory.py"], "defects": [{"file": "inventory.py", "line": 8, "explanation": "Dividing by len(sales) raises ZeroDivisionError when the sales list is empty, and nothing guards against that case."}, {"file": "inventory.py", "line": 21, "explanation": "The loop starts at index 1, so low_stock never checks the first item and misses it even when its stock is below the threshold."}, {"file": "report.py", "line": 5, "explanation": "The file is opened without a context manager and never closed, so the written summary may not be flushed to disk and the file handle leaks."}]}

{"step": 2, "files": ["report.py", "README.md", "inventory.py"], "defects": [{"file": "inventory.py", "line": 8, "explanation": "There is no error handling for an empty sales list, so average_daily_sales and its caller reorder_quantity raise an unhandled ZeroDivisionError."}, {"file": "inventory.py", "line": 6, "explanation": "The loop on lines 5-7 rebuilds the built-in sum() by hand, which adds needless code where sum(sales) would do."}, {"file": "inventory.py", "line": 21, "explanation": "The loop walks indices with range() instead of iterating over items directly, and the off-by-one start index this allows skips the first item."}, {"file": "report.py", "line": 5, "explanation": "open() is called without a with-block or try/finally, so the file is never closed and an exception during writing leaves a partly written, unflushed file."}]}
